verdict.rationale: PostHog Desktop's own docs say agents running in the app can use "Other MCP servers for services such as issue trackers, design tools, and internal APIs," so the product does act as an MCP client. That support is a single line, and the agents involved are third-party (Pi, Claude Code, Codex), so it is unclear how much of the client capability is PostHog's own. The extensive evidence for PostHog's hosted MCP server covers the server role and does not count toward this story. Missing for 10: documentation on how to add or configure external MCP servers in Desktop, evidence that PostHog AI in the web app or the Slack agent can use third-party MCP tools, details on transport, auth or tool scoping for connected servers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools
